targets.text: The Thor gives up its local Qwen3.8 cortex and serves Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4 as the mesh's worker arm, on a Thor-MEASURED recipe rather than a copied one

falsifiable on the deployed box: model=worker answers 200 on the Thor's own gateway serving the nvidia 35B-A3B id, model=cortex no longer resolves locally there, and an acceptance transcript exists under docs/evidence/

lobes/catalog.py gains a NEW SupportedModel for nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 — it is absent today (catalog holds unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 at :805-895, demoted to role_hint='candidate' at :866, and mmangkad/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 at :391-408). role_hint is effectively unique: roles._catalog_by_role_hint (roles.py:548-550) returns the FIRST match, so promoting the nvidia entry to role_hint='worker' REQUIRES demoting the Nemotron Lightning entry (catalog.py:986) — and 'associate' shares ROLE_ROLE_HINT='worker' (roles.py:169), so the Orin's associate catalog default moves with it

the committed catalog entry's native_max_model_len / quantization / speculative_config / tool_parser are read from the checkpoint's own config.json + hf_quant_config.json at implementation time, not from the model card or this frame; and tests/test_catalog.py still passes its role_hint-uniqueness and parser-pairing guards

the issue's 15-flag recipe does NOT fit today's vllm-worker lane: docker-compose.yml:1501-1513 emits only --quantization/--max-model-len/--gpu-memory-utilization/--enable-auto-tool-choice plus two env-carried slots (WORKER_SPECULATIVE_CONFIG :1509, default-OFF; WORKER_REASONING_PARSER :1512, default nemotron_v3). NINE flags are not expressible without a template change — --kv-cache-dtype, --attention-backend, --moe-backend, --max-num-seqs, --max-num-batched-tokens, --enable-chunked-prefill, --async-scheduling, --enable-prefix-caching, --load-format — and --tool-call-parser=qwen3_coder is HARDCODED at :1511, so the issue's qwen3_xml is not selectable at all

the flags actually added to the vllm-worker lane are exactly the ones an arm needed to run — each new knob traceable to a measured arm — and a rendered deployment with none of them set stays byte-identical to today's goldens

a recipe knob must land in BOTH the profile schema and the compose command or it is inert: schema.py KNOB_NAMES (:81-107) has no moe_backend/load_format/async_scheduling/chunked_prefill/prefix_caching/max_num_batched_tokens field, while WORKER_KV_CACHE_DTYPE / WORKER_ATTENTION_BACKEND / WORKER_MAX_NUM_SEQS ARE renderable (render.py:109-141 x ROLE_ENV_PREFIX:94) yet read by nothing on the worker lane — dead keys today (env.example:498 says WORKER_ATTENTION_BACKEND is deliberately unwired). There is no *_EXTRA_ARGS escape hatch anywhere; the only documented route for an unwired flag is hand-editing the rendered compose (switch.py:170-177 _moe_notice), which is exactly what issue #214 and the deployment lock exist to stop

every knob this work adds is reachable end-to-end: declared in schema.py, rendered by render.py, read by the compose command, and covered by a golden; no knob ships that renders a key nothing consumes

--moe-backend marlin (the issue's headline Thor recommendation) was MEASURED REFUSED on this box: docs/evidence/2026-07-31-accept-worker-thor.txt:5-11 records marlin 'not supported for unquantized MoE', flashinfer_b12x/flashinfer_cutlass 'kernel does not support current device cuda' (sm_121a/Spark-only), triton 'not supported for NvFP4 MoE' — only AUTO-SELECT booted, and thor-worker.toml:49-58 carries that as a standing rule. The nvidia export excludes mtp* from quantization too (c3), so the recorded refusal reason plausibly reproduces. Marlin is therefore a HYPOTHESIS to be accepted or refused live on the Thor, never a copied default

the moe-backend question is settled by a live Thor boot, and whichever way it lands is committed with its verbatim engine error or success line in the evidence transcript — including the case where marlin is refused again for the same recorded reason

61.2 tok/s is NOT a like-for-like acceptance threshold: docs/evidence/2026-08-20-baseline-worker-qwen35b-thor.txt:1-28 measured it on the PHYSICAL Thor but with the unsloth export, the OLD 0.23.1rc1.dev672 engine (the fleet has since moved to 8bd082), util 0.45 / 262144, self-draft MTP on — a different checkpoint AND a different engine from this issue's target. The earlier 2026-07-31 acceptance on the same box read 50.8 tok/s with thinking / 73.5 without, MTP acceptance 89.1%. Per docs/model-switch-playbook.md the incumbent must be re-baselined same-day/same-harness rather than compared against an older figure

no doc or PR body compares this lane against 61.2 tok/s without naming that the figure came from a different checkpoint on a different engine; the comparison the acceptance rests on is a same-day, same-harness measurement

the measurement the issue demands does not exist yet: roles_measure.LLM_METRIC_KEYS (:79-89) carries no acceptance field; the only acceptance surface is scripts/spec-arms.py — NOT a registered lobes verb — which scrapes vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted/draft_tokens_total or greps the engine's SpecDecoding log line, both ENGINE-WIDE not per-request (:64-81), and its regex (:283-288) DROPS the per-position acceptance array vLLM already prints. Single-stream vs aggregate separation exists only in 'lobes benchmark --all-lobes --concurrency' (benchmark.py:69-133,383-390) and has never been pointed at a spec-arm sweep (docs/dspark-speculation.md:308)

the acceptance numbers the sweep reports come from a repeatable harness committed in-tree (a verb or a committed script), not from a hand-run one-off, and the per-depth acceptance figures are read from vLLM's own metrics or log line rather than inferred from throughput

the Thor does NOT render the thor-worker shape today — it renders spark-lobe (docs/evidence/2026-08-20-accept-cortex-local-thor.txt:8, re-confirmed docs/specs/2026-08-25-thor-cortex-speculation.md:52,69), which is why it serves cortex locally. thor-worker.toml still declares the OLD unsloth model at util 0.45 / 262144 (:79-84) and hosts ['worker','hand','embedder','reranker','stt','tts'] (:70) — including hand, which thor.toml:109 declares feasible=false on this card. Re-arming worker here means re-pointing that shape (or adding one) and moving four goldens: tests/goldens/shapes/thor-worker__{base,orin,spark,thor}.env

the shape change is byte-for-byte visible: the four thor-worker__*.env goldens are regenerated and reviewed for cross-machine bleed, and the shape TOML's committed budget is the value a live Thor boot measured, with any refused hypothesis recorded in its comments

'worker-fast' cannot be a second role or alias without new surface: Shape.overrides is one RoleProfile per role name (shapes.py:176,186-195), SHAPE_ROLES is a flat fixed vocabulary that REJECTS an unknown override key (shapes.py:135,247-256), schema.ROLES is a fixed nine-name tuple (:57-76), and OPT_IN_CORE_ACTIVATION_ENV / OPT_IN_CORE_COMPOSE_PROFILE map each role 1:1 to one compose service and one base URL (shape_render.py:139-165). So the reliable/fast split must ship as two SHAPES (or two env recipes) over the one worker role — matching the issue's own 'keep worker stable, do not silently replace the default'
callers keep addressing model=worker throughout: no new role name, no new tier, no new public alias appears in lobes capabilities, GET /capabilities or /v1/models as a result of the fast profile

giving up Thor's local cortex is not free, and the cost is MEASURED, not theoretical: the Spark+Thor cortex replica pool is the one VALIDATED #199 deployment (docs/gateway-fleet.md:757-780 — 19.1 tok/s aggregate vs an 11.0 single-owner baseline, +74%, plus peer-down continuity), and the Orin hosts no cortex at all, reaching it through a peer-only pool that declares BOTH boxes (docs/gateway-fleet.md:797-800,860-870). Dropping cortex on the Thor collapses the pool to single-owner and leaves the Orin with one replica

the pool teardown is executed deliberately and recorded: the Spark's and Orin's PRIMARY_PEER_* declarations are updated in the same change window, and a probe from each box after the change shows cortex still served (by the Spark) with no 5xx and no stale hosted_by

flipping the Thor's cortex to infeasible has a STARTUP TRAP, not just a throughput cost: server.py:3981-4028 (_check_pool_arming) requires any DROPPED role that still declares the plural PRIMARY_PEER_ORIGINS to ALSO declare the singular PRIMARY_PEER_ORIGIN, else build_replica_caches raises a named ReplicaConfigError and the gateway refuses to boot — and the deployed Thor .env declares PRIMARY_PEER_ORIGINS=http://spark... today with no singular origin. Separately, gateway/_config.py:60's _DEFAULT_WORKER is STALE ('unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4'), so an unset WORKER_SERVED_NAME already advertises a checkpoint no box serves
the Thor's gateway boots after the flip — proving _check_pool_arming is satisfied — and an unset WORKER_SERVED_NAME no longer advertises a checkpoint no box serves

worker and associate sharing ROLE_ROLE_HINT='worker' (roles.py:169) is a DEFECT to fix in this work, not a constraint to design around: they are different roles with different contracts (associate = worker minus repo_action), and the shared catalog role_hint means promoting a worker checkpoint silently moves the Orin's associate default with it. Give associate its own role_hint / catalog resolution

the split is proven by a test, not by inspection: a test asserts that changing the checkpoint on role_hint='worker' leaves the model 'associate' resolves to unchanged, and lobes capabilities on the Orin still names its own associate checkpoint after the worker promotion

the operator running the three physical boxes (Thor, Spark, Orin), plus every mesh consumer that addresses model=worker through a gateway — and the next engineer who reads a Thor recipe in this repo and needs to know which numbers were measured here and which were copied from a vendor page

the evidence transcript and the per-model doc are written so an operator can re-run the recipe from them alone: image digest, JetPack/L4T, power mode, clocks, co-resident set and the exact argv are all present

the Thor serves nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 as 'worker' at a Thor-MEASURED budget, reached from any box as model=worker; cortex is gone from this box; the vllm-worker lane can express the recipe knobs the measurement needed (not all fifteen — the ones the arms proved matter); a docs/evidence/ transcript records single-stream decode separately from concurrent throughput and records MTP acceptance per depth; and a second, named fast profile exists only if its gain was measured and repeatable
each item is checked against the merged tree and the live box, and anything that did not land is reported as not landed in the delivery summary rather than quietly dropped

the Thor renders spark-lobe and serves cortex locally at 262144/util 0.58 (12.1 tok/s single-stream); WORKER_FEASIBLE=false, model=worker 404s role_infeasible on every gateway in the mesh, and the catalog's worker seat holds a checkpoint (Nemotron Lightning) that is a recorded NO-GO on this board. The nvidia 35B-A3B export exists in no catalog entry and has never been booted on any box in this fleet
the before-state is captured as a transcript BEFORE the flip — the cortex figures on this box are unrecoverable afterwards, exactly the trap docs/model-switch-playbook.md records

the mesh trades cortex concurrency for execution speed on purpose: the Thor's dense 27B decodes at 12.1 tok/s, while a ~3B-active MoE on this same board measured 61.2 tok/s on an older engine — a fast doer is worth more here than a second cortex replica, and the operator has accepted the pool loss (q1). The aim is 100 tok/s single-stream on this board, which is ~1.6x the best figure ever measured here and is NOT expected from the reliable MTP lane alone — reaching it is what the fast gear (deeper MTP or DFlash) has to earn. The speed claim is the whole point, so it is measured single-stream on this box or it is not claimed
the forum and vendor throughput figures (190.7 / 239.1 / 116.5 tok/s) appear only as external references with their source named, never as this repo's acceptance thresholds

on the deployed Thor: model=worker answers 200 through the gateway with a tool call parsed into tool_calls (not content) and a separated reasoning trace; MTP is measured at k = off/1/3/5/7 with acceptance recorded per depth; and a peer box reaches the lane as model=worker with X-Lobes-Proxied-By. The THROUGHPUT TARGET is 100 tok/s single-stream decode on this box, with 61.2 tok/s (the old Thor figure) as the floor: below 61.2 is a regression and blocks acceptance; 61.2-100 is accepted only with the gap measured and the next lever named; at or above 100 the target is met. Concurrent throughput is reported separately and never substituted for the single-stream number

every listed signal is a checkable artifact: a chat transcript with a parsed tool_calls array, a docs/evidence/ file with the decode and acceptance tables, and a cross-box response carrying X-Lobes-Proxied-By

the Thor is not a lobes-only box: docker ps on it (2026-09-10) shows the Culture PRODUCTION stack co-resident — prod-postgres, prod-minio, prod-api, prod-scheduler, prod-worker, prod-notifier — alongside the lobes lanes, and every container is restart=unless-stopped. Any box-level action this work takes (a JetPack 7.2 upgrade, a reboot to reclaim leaked memory, a driver change) takes production down with it, so box-level moves are operator-scheduled events, never a step inside an arm loop
no step in this work stops, restarts or reboots the box without the operator scheduling it, and the production stack is verified running again afterwards

the arm loop needs memory-reclaim discipline, because THIS box has already lost ~80 GiB to a failed worker boot: on 2026-08-11 a CUDA 'unspecified launch failure' in vLLM's startup KV-cache profiling killed model-gear-vllm-worker with a clean exit 0 and leaked unified memory no process owned (nvidia-smi reports no devices on Jetson, so it is unattributable from userspace) — only a reboot reclaimed it. Between arms: drop caches BEFORE any heavy-lobe recreate, read tegrastats rather than MemAvailable or docker stats, and diagnose a leak by summing ps RSS against free
the transcript records free/tegrastats before and after every arm, and any unexplained memory gap is reported rather than worked around

the gateway restart step must neutralise the Thor's inbound-key trap: this box's ~/.bashrc exports GATEWAY_API_KEY (the Spark's key) and docker compose interpolates shell env AHEAD of .env, so an ssh-driven 'docker compose up gateway' silently ARMS the inbound gate and every subsequent request 401s. Every compose invocation in this work runs as 'env -u GATEWAY_API_KEY docker compose ...'
an unauthenticated probe after each gateway restart returns what the deployment intends — never an accidental 401

with cortex gone, this box needs a stated answer for the pressure floor: hand is declared feasible=false on the Thor (thor.toml:109), and worker sheds 429 under swap/iowait pressure exactly like cortex/senses/muse — so after the flip the Thor has NO servable generate floor and a pressure event turns every local generate request into a 429 with no cheaper rung. Either hand becomes feasible here, or the shape declares the floor's absence deliberately and the docs say so
after the flip, a pressure event on this box produces the documented behaviour: either a served hand response or a 429 that the docs already say to expect

declare WORKER_SPECULATIVE_CONFIG in .env rather than only in the compose command, so the lane's speculation is visible in the /capabilities fingerprint: issue #214 recorded exactly this lie on the cortex lanes — two boxes drafting differently (DSpark vs MTP) both reported speculative_config: unknown because neither declared the key. A worker arm sweep that changes drafting per arm is worthless as evidence if the advert cannot say which arm is live
each arm's /capabilities fingerprint names the speculative config that docker inspect proves is loaded

the flip needs a rollout note and a raw-id audit, because per docs/model-switch-playbook.md no consumer in this mesh addresses the fleet by role name: dropping cortex from the Thor 404s every raw-id pinner that dials THIS box's gateway, silently and instantly. The precedent artifact is docs/worker-lightning-rollout-notes.md — the same note, written for this flip, addressed to every pinner the audit finds
the rollout note exists before the flip and names every raw-id consumer the audit found, including the ones running on this box

back up the deployment dir and record the restore path before touching it: ~/.lobes on this box already carries two hand-edited compose backups (docker-compose.yml.bak-moe, .bak-20260828-161830), which is precisely the drift #214 was filed for, and the shape contract's byte-for-byte restorability only holds for a render, not for a hand-edit. The rollback to cortex-local is 're-render the previous shape and restore the saved .env', proven by restoring it once in a dry run before the flip is committed
the reverse render is dry-run and shown to reproduce the pre-flip deployment before the forward flip is applied

serving worker multimodal is a LANE fact, not just a contract fact: the vllm-worker command must NOT pass --language-model-only (the unsloth worker era omitted it deliberately and validated image+video intake live), and image intake on worker has to be probed on this box before the widened responsibilities are advertised — a role that declares image_understanding and then 400s on an image is exactly the lie #108 forbids
capabilities lists image_understanding/video_understanding for worker only after a live image probe on this box passed with a negative control

widening worker does not make it senses: this box declares MULTIMODAL_FEASIBLE=false and proxies model=senses to the Orin, and that stays true — worker gaining vision adds a second local vision-capable lane, it does not re-host the senses role or change what model=senses resolves to anywhere in the mesh
after the flip model=senses on the Thor still resolves to the Orin peer, byte-identically to today

risks.text: the checkpoint may not load at all on the pinned nightly on sm_110 — the fleet's own doc records why it serves the mmangkad copy rather than nvidia's; t11 is the gate and a NO-GO there stops the plan rather than substituting a different export

risks.resolution: RESOLVED — the target was MET, not missed: MTP n=3 measured ~129.0 tok/s single-stream median (112.89/129.02/132.46 over three identical code prompts) against the 100 tok/s target, with 93.2% engine-wide acceptance and per-position 1.000/0.943/0.874. Unspeculated ARM A measured ~68.5 tok/s, already above the 61.2 floor. Same-day incumbent cortex on the same box: 18.7 tok/s.
